title: Icon 10CS: how a long-lasting residual spray works at home
description: How Syngenta Icon 10CS keeps working after it dries, where to spray it against mosquitoes, flies and cockroaches in Kenya, and what to do first.
answer: Icon 10CS is a long-lasting residual insecticide. Dilute it as the label directs, spray the surfaces where mosquitoes, flies and cockroaches rest or walk, and it keeps releasing its active ingredient after the spray has dried. Treat the whole house in one session and clear standing water first.
intro: Mbu (mosquitoes) bite at dusk and through the night, and they can carry diseases such as malaria. A spray that works only while it is wet means spraying again and again, which is why a residual insecticide is worth understanding before you buy one.

sections.heading: What does capsule suspension mean?
paragraphs: Syngenta Icon 10CS contains lambda-cyhalothrin in a capsule suspension (CS) formulation. The active ingredient is held in tiny capsules in a liquid. After spraying, the capsules stay on the treated surface and release the active ingredient slowly.
This is designed to give a longer-lasting residual effect than a spray that acts all at once, so insects that land on or walk across the surface keep picking up the insecticide.

sections.heading: Where should I spray it?
paragraphs: Think about where insects rest or walk, not only where you see them. Icon 10CS is sold for mosquitoes, flies and cockroaches in homes and small businesses, so focus on these places:
bullets: Walls, and door and window frames
Eaves and shaded places
Drains and damp corners
Cracks and corners where cockroaches hide

sections.heading: What should I do before and after spraying?
paragraphs: Treat the whole house in one session so insects do not simply move to an untreated room. Remove or cover food, dishes and water containers, and keep people and pets out of the treated rooms until the spray has dried.
Clearing stagnant water, rubbish and blocked drains removes breeding sites, and mosquito nets and window screens add protection while you sleep.
Keep any leftover concentrate in the original closed bottle, in a cool, dry, locked place away from food and feed.

Wear gloves, a mask, goggles and protective clothing when you mix and spray, and wash well afterwards. Lambda-cyhalothrin is very toxic to fish and bees, so never rinse sprayers or containers into drains, streams, ponds or fish tanks.

faq: Is the 62.5 ml pack enough for my house?
It is a convenient size for a house, a few rooms or a small business. A large building may need more than one pack, or a licensed pest control operator.
Do I need to dilute Icon 10CS?
Yes. Shake the bottle well, measure carefully and mix it thoroughly in clean water in the sprayer, as the label directs.
Does a residual spray replace nets and clean-up?
No. Use it together with mosquito nets, window screens and the removal of stagnant water and rubbish.
closing: See the [[/p/icon-10cs-mosquito-insecticide-62-5-ml.html|Icon 10CS product page]], browse [[/c/mosquito-fly-control.html|mosquito and fly control]], or read our [[/blog/mosquito-control-at-home-kenya.html|mosquito control guide]].

title: Single-feed rat bait: how Bayer Baraki pellets are used
description: Bayer Baraki pellets need to be eaten only once. See which pack suits a home, shop or farm in Kenya, where to place bait stations and how often to check.
answer: Bayer Baraki is a ready-to-use single-feed bait: rats and mice need to eat it only once. Place it in covered bait stations along walls, runs and burrows, check every 2 to 3 days and top up until feeding stops. Choose the 10 g, 100 g or 1 kg pack to match your number of stations.
intro: A rodent problem rarely stays small. Rats gnaw wiring, foul food stores and spread disease, and a few quickly become many. Baraki is made for single-feed control, which means rats and mice need to eat the bait only once.

sections.heading: What does single-feed mean?
paragraphs: Baraki pellets contain difethialone, an anticoagulant, in a ready-to-use bait that needs no mixing. Single-feed means a rodent needs to eat the bait only once, so you are not relying on it returning to the same spot many times.
The pellets resist mould and moisture, which keeps them attractive in damp stores, and Baraki is sold as effective against resistant strains.

sections.heading: Where should the bait stations go?
paragraphs: Three species behave differently. Roof rats climb into ceilings and stores, Norway rats burrow along walls and drains, and house mice nest in small hidden spaces. Inspect for droppings, gnaw marks, runs and burrows first, so you know where they travel.
Put the bait in covered bait stations or tamper-resistant boxes, never loose on the floor. Baraki's placement amounts are:
bullets: Rats: 50 to 75 g per station, one station every 5 to 10 m along walls, rat runs, burrows and sheltered areas
Mice: 15 to 20 g per station, one station every 2 to 4 m along walls, runways and nests

sections.heading: Which pack size should I buy?
paragraphs: The 10 g sachet suits one room or a first trial. The 100 g pack, about ten sachets, suits a shop, a store or a home with several bait points. The 1 kg box, about a hundred sachets, suits farms, markets and industrial sites. Count your stations first, because the amounts above show how much bait each one holds.

Bait does more when it is paired with proofing. Block holes and gaps around pipes, doors and roof edges, keep grain and food in closed containers off the floor, and remove the rubbish and clutter that give rodents shelter.

faq: How often should I check the stations?
Every 2 to 3 days, topping up until feeding stops. Read the label on your pack as well.
Does Baraki need mixing?
No. The pellets are ready to use, so you simply place them in covered bait stations.
What do I do with dead rodents?
Wearing gloves, collect them and dispose of them safely, then wash your hands. Keep the bait away from children, pets and poultry.
closing: See the [[/p/bayer-baraki-pellets-rat-and-mice-poison-10-g.html|Bayer Baraki product page]] for every size, browse [[/c/rodent-control.html|rodent control]], or read our [[/blog/rat-and-mouse-control-kenya.html|rat and mouse control guide]].

title: Bromarat 0.005 RB: setting up bait stations for rats and mice
description: Why Bromarat 0.005 RB rodent bait goes inside bait stations, where to put them in a home, shop or store in Kenya, and how long to keep baiting.
answer: Bromarat 0.005 RB is a ready-to-use rodent bait made for bait stations. Fill the stations, place them along walls, near holes and on runs where you see droppings, check them regularly and keep baiting until no more is taken. Choose 25 g for a home or small store, 100 g for larger premises.
intro: Loose bait on the floor is easy to scatter and easy for a child or a pet to find. A bait station solves that, and Bromarat 0.005 RB is sold for use inside one. There is nothing to mix, so the real work is in the placing.

sections.heading: Why use a bait station at all?
paragraphs: A bait station is a small covered box or tube that holds the bait. It keeps the bait dry and clean, makes it harder for children, pets and livestock to reach it, and gives rodents a dark, sheltered place where they feel safe to feed.
Stations also show you how much has been eaten, so you learn where the rodents are most active.

sections.heading: Where do the stations go?
paragraphs: Walk around the building first and look for droppings, gnaw marks and runs. Then place stations along walls, near holes and burrows, behind cupboards and stacked goods, and on the runs themselves. A home or small shop usually needs a few. A store or farm needs more, spaced as the label advises.
Prepare the site at the same time:
bullets: Keep food and grain in closed containers and stack bags away from the walls
Block holes around pipes and doors
Clear rubbish and long grass near the building

sections.heading: How long should I keep baiting?
paragraphs: Check the stations regularly, top up bait that has been eaten and replace bait that is wet or mouldy. Carry on until no more bait is taken, then remove the stations and the leftover bait as the label directs.

Keep the stations and the pack away from food, feed and drinking water, wear gloves, and wash your hands afterwards. Check the PCPB registration number on the label, and store the pack tightly closed in a cool, dry, locked place out of reach of children and pets.

faq: Which Bromarat pack suits my building?
The 25 g pack suits a home or a small shop with a few stations. The 100 g pack suits stores, farms and larger premises with many.
Does Bromarat need mixing?
No. It is ready to use, so you fill the stations and place them where the rodents travel.
What if an animal eats the bait?
If an animal eats it, call a vet. If anyone swallows the bait, get medical help at once and show the label.
closing: See the [[/p/bromarat-0-005-rb-rodent-bait-25-g.html|Bromarat 0.005 RB product page]], browse [[/c/rodent-control.html|rodent control]], or read our [[/blog/rat-and-mouse-control-kenya.html|rat and mouse control guide]].

title: Moles (fuko) and rats on a small farm: using Fuko-Kil
description: Fuko-Kil is sold for rats and moles. See how moles damage young plants, where the 25 g pack fits on a small farm or garden in Kenya, and the safety rules.
answer: Fuko-Kil is a rodenticide sold for rats and moles in homes, stores and farms. Follow the label for placement and quantity, put bait in protected spots or active runs rather than on the soil surface, and keep it away from children, pets and poultry. The 25 g pack suits a limited area.
intro: Moles (fuko) rarely show themselves. What you see is the mounds of soil and the tunnels through a lawn, garden or field. Rats are easier to spot but just as costly in a store, which is why Fuko-Kil is sold for both.

sections.heading: How do moles and rats cause damage?
paragraphs: Moles push up mounds of soil and cut tunnels through lawns, gardens and fields. They damage the roots of young plants, which matters most on small farms and in kitchen gardens where young plants have shallow roots.
Rats eat and spoil stored food, gnaw wires, packaging and furniture, and spread germs through droppings and urine. They breed fast, so a small problem soon becomes a large one.

sections.heading: How is Fuko-Kil placed for each pest?
paragraphs: The label decides placement and quantity, and the method differs for each animal. Look for fresh mounds and runs first, so you know where the moles are active.
bullets: Rats: small amounts of bait in protected spots near nesting holes, along walls and on runs where you see droppings and gnaw marks, in a covered tray or bait station where possible
Moles: place the product in active runs as the label directs, and never spread it on the soil surface where other animals could find it

sections.heading: What should I do around the bait?
paragraphs: Check the PCPB registration number on the label and read it before use. Keep Fuko-Kil away from children, pets, poultry and other animals, and never place it where food, feed or water can be contaminated.

Replace bait that has been eaten or has got wet, and stop when the activity ends. Collect dead rodents regularly, wearing gloves, and remove leftover bait at the end of the treatment as the label directs.

faq: Can Fuko-Kil be used for both rats and moles?
It is sold for rats and moles. Placement differs for each, so follow the label for rats in buildings and for moles in active runs.
Is the 25 g pack enough?
It is a small pack for a home or a small farm treating a limited area. A large store or farm will need more bait than one pack.
What if a pet or another animal eats the bait?
Contact a vet immediately. If a person swallows it, get medical help at once and show the pack.
closing: See the [[/p/fuko-kil-rat-poison-25-g.html|Fuko-Kil product page]], browse [[/c/rodent-control.html|rodent control]], or read our [[/blog/rat-and-mouse-control-kenya.html|rat and mouse control guide]].

title: Miratex rat and mice bait: choosing the 20 g or 240 g pack
description: Miratex pellets come in 20 g and 240 g packs. See which suits a room, a shop or a warehouse in Kenya, and how to count bait points before you order.
answer: Choose the 20 g pack for a single room, a small store or a first treatment, and the 240 g pack for warehouses, hotels, farms and other larger premises with many bait points. Miratex pellets are ready to use, so count your bait points first, then place them near droppings, along walls and near nesting holes.
intro: Buying rat bait by pack size alone is a guess. A single room and a godown need very different quantities, so it helps to decide how many bait points you need before you choose between the two Miratex packs.

sections.heading: Which Miratex pack fits my premises?
paragraphs: The 20 g pack suits a single room, a kitchen, a small store or a first treatment, so you can start small and see what the activity tells you. The 240 g pack is made for warehouses, hotels, farms and other larger premises that need many bait points.
Larger buildings need bait in many places and need it topped up over time. Think of grain stores, feed stores, poultry houses, workshops and godowns.

sections.heading: How do I count the bait points I need?
paragraphs: Walk around first and look for droppings, gnaw marks, greasy rub marks along walls and burrows. Rodents usually move along walls and through dark, quiet corners, so bait close to those signs works better than bait in the middle of a room.

Count the points before you choose a size, because a pack that runs out halfway through a building leaves gaps. Wear gloves, and remove dead rodents safely. Store the pellets in their closed pack, somewhere dry and secure, away from food and out of reach of children.

sections.heading: What should I do before placing the pellets?
paragraphs: Pellets need no mixing, but they do more alongside good hygiene, because rodents contaminate food, chew wires and damage sacks and furniture wherever food is easy to find.
bullets: Keep grain and animal feed in sealed containers, on raised pallets in stores
Block holes and gaps, and cut tall grass close to buildings
Keep rubbish and old materials away from the walls

faq: Do I need to mix the pellets?
No. They are ready to use, so you place them directly at the bait points.
Where do rats usually travel?
Along walls, through dark corners and between their nest and their food. Bait close to droppings, gnaw marks and runways works better than bait in the middle of a room.
Where must I keep the bait away from?
Place it where only rodents can reach it, never near food for people or animals and never inside food containers. Keep it away from children, pets and livestock.
closing: See the [[/p/miratex-pellets-rat-and-mice-killer-bait-20-g.html|Miratex pellets product page]] for both sizes, browse [[/c/rodent-control.html|rodent control]], or read our [[/blog/rat-and-mouse-control-kenya.html|rat and mouse control guide]].

title: Rat poison for a house or small shop: starting with Rat-Kill
description: A small 25 g pack of Rat-Kill pellets is a low-commitment way to start rat control in a home, kitchen or small shop in Kenya. See where to place it.
answer: Rat-Kill pellets are a ready-to-use bait for rats and mice in homes, shops, stores and farms. The small 25 g pack suits a single room, a kitchen or a small shop. Place the pellets close to droppings, along walls and near nesting holes, out of reach of children, pets and livestock.
intro: Few people want a large pack of poison for one kitchen. Rat-Kill is sold in a small 25 g pack, sized for a single room, a kitchen, a small shop or a first treatment, so you can start without buying more than you need.

sections.heading: What does the 25 g pack cover?
paragraphs: Think of it as a first treatment for a small space. There is no mixing and no sprayer, so you place the pellets directly where you see rodent activity.
If the problem turns out to be bigger than one room, a store or a farm will need a larger rodent bait. That is the sign to plan more bait points.

sections.heading: Where do I place the pellets?
paragraphs: Look for droppings, gnaw marks, greasy rub marks along walls and holes where rodents live and travel. Place the bait close to those signs, along walls and near nesting holes, in places that children, pets and livestock cannot reach.

Pick your bait spots before you open the pack, so the pellets go down quickly and stay out of reach. Check the bait often, replace bait that has been eaten and remove dead rodents safely, wearing gloves.
Close the pack after each use and keep it out of reach, in a cool, dry cupboard or store that can be locked.

sections.heading: What should I fix at the same time?
paragraphs: Baiting and hygiene work together. Rats and mice eat and spoil stored food, gnaw electrical wires and spread disease through droppings and urine, and they breed quickly, so a few can become a large problem within weeks.
bullets: Cover food and keep grain and feed in sealed containers
Block holes and gaps around pipes, doors and floors
Keep the area clean and free of crumbs and spilled feed

faq: Where can I buy rat poison in Kenya?
Order Rat-Kill pellets online, pay by M-Pesa and get delivery to all 47 counties, or pick up at The Sarit Centre in Westlands, Nairobi.
Do I need to mix Rat-Kill pellets with anything?
No. The pellets are ready to use, so you place them directly where you see rodent activity.
What safety steps should I take?
Check the PCPB registration number on the label and read it before use. Keep the pellets where other animals cannot reach them, and wash your hands after handling.
closing: See the [[/p/rat-kill-pellets-25-g.html|Rat-Kill pellets product page]], browse [[/c/rodent-control.html|rodent control]], or read our [[/blog/rat-and-mouse-control-kenya.html|rat and mouse control guide]].

title: Rat control in a warehouse or store: planning with Rodent-Kill
description: How property managers, farmers and shopkeepers in Kenya can plan rat baiting in a warehouse, godown or farm store with the 500 g Rodent-Kill pack.
answer: In a large building, walk the whole site first and mark droppings and gnaw marks. Then place covered bait stations along walls, behind stacked goods, near holes and on rat runs. Rodent-Kill is a ready-to-use rat pellet bait, and its 500 g pack is made for premises that need many bait points.
intro: A big building gives rats plenty of places to hide, breed and feed. Baiting one corner of a godown does little when the nest is behind the next stack, so the work starts with a plan rather than a pack.

sections.heading: Why does a large building need a plan?
paragraphs: Infestations in large buildings are brought under control by baiting many points and keeping them topped up as the rodents feed. The 500 g size gives you the quantity to do that without running short halfway, which suits property managers, farmers, shopkeepers and stores that treat regularly.
Grain stores, feed stores, godowns, hotels and poultry houses are the usual places. Pellets need no mixing, so a caretaker can fill stations quickly on a round of the building.

sections.heading: How do I lay out the bait stations?
paragraphs: Use covered bait stations so that only rodents can reach the bait. Wear gloves when you handle it, and never place bait on food surfaces or near food for people or livestock. Put stations in these places:
bullets: Along walls and behind stacked goods
Near holes and on rat runs
Wherever you marked droppings and gnaw marks on your first walk-round

sections.heading: What should I do besides baiting?
paragraphs: Baiting is strongest when it is paired with good sanitation and proofing. Inspect the stations often, replace bait that has been eaten and collect dead rodents carefully so that pets and wildlife do not feed on them.
bullets: Store grain, feed and produce on raised pallets away from walls
Seal holes and gaps, and keep drains covered
Remove rubbish and clutter
Cut grass and bush near the buildings

faq: Who is the 500 g pack for?
It is for warehouses, stores and farm buildings where many bait points are needed, such as grain stores, feed stores, godowns, hotels and poultry houses.
Where should the bait stations go?
Along walls, behind stacked goods, near holes and on rat runs, in covered stations that only rodents can reach.
How should I store the rest of the pack?
Reseal the pack after filling the stations and keep the rest in a locked, dry, cool store, apart from feed and food. Read the label and check the PCPB registration number before use.
closing: See the [[/p/rodent-kill-rat-pellets-500-g.html|Rodent-Kill product page]], browse [[/c/rodent-control.html|rodent control]], or read our [[/blog/rat-and-mouse-control-kenya.html|rat and mouse control guide]].

title: Rat bait for damp places: when Rodilon wax blocks make sense
description: Loose pellets can go mouldy in damp stores. See where Rodilon wax blocks hold up better in Kenya, how to place them above wet floors and what to fix first.
answer: Use wax blocks where moisture would spoil loose pellets: basements, drains, cellars, stores near the kitchen, farm sheds and poultry houses. Rodilon blocks are made to hold up in damp, humid places. Put them along walls and near holes, above the wet floor where possible, in covered bait stations.
intro: Ordinary baits can soften, grow mould or lose their appeal when they get wet. If your rat problem is in a damp corner, the form of the bait matters as much as the brand name on the pack.

sections.heading: Why do wax blocks suit damp areas?
paragraphs: Wax blocks are made to resist moisture, so they stay in good condition for longer in basements, drains, cellars, stores near the kitchen, farm sheds and poultry houses.
Rats and mice can gnaw the blocks, and because a block is solid it is also useful where pellets might be carried off or scattered.

sections.heading: Where should I put the blocks?
paragraphs: Put blocks along walls, near holes and burrows, behind appliances and in dark corners where you see droppings or gnaw marks. In a damp area, keep them above the wet floor where you can.

Use covered bait stations that keep out children, pets and livestock, check them often and replace any block that has been eaten or damaged. The 10 g pack is a small size for kitchens, drains, small stores and sheds, so you can bait one trouble spot without buying a large pack.
Keep the blocks away from children, pets and livestock, and check the PCPB registration number on the label before use. Collect dead rodents with gloves and dispose of them safely.

sections.heading: What fixes the damp problem itself?
paragraphs: Bait is only half of the answer, because rodents come for water as well as food. Deal with the conditions that bring them in:
bullets: Fix leaking pipes that give rodents water
Store grain and feed in sealed containers
Block gaps around pipes, doors and roofs
Keep rubbish covered and take it out regularly

faq: Why choose a wax block instead of pellets?
Blocks are made to resist moisture, so they hold up in damp places where loose pellets can go mouldy or spoil quickly.
Where can I use Rodilon blocks?
They are sold for rats and mice in damp areas, stores and farms, including kitchens, drains, small stores and sheds.
How do I handle and store the blocks?
Wear gloves to handle them and wash your hands afterwards. Keep unused blocks in their pack, dry and out of reach, away from food and animal feed.
closing: See the [[/p/rodilon-wax-blocks-10-g.html|Rodilon wax blocks product page]], browse [[/c/rodent-control.html|rodent control]], or read our [[/blog/rat-and-mouse-control-kenya.html|rat and mouse control guide]].

title: Rat control in a poultry house: using Tatua bait blocks safely
description: Rodents steal feed and disturb birds. See how Syngenta Tatua rat and mice poison blocks are fixed inside bait stations in poultry houses, stores and farms.
answer: Use Syngenta Tatua bait blocks only inside bait stations. Find where rodents travel from droppings, gnaw marks and runways, put stations along walls and near holes, and keep the blocks away from feed, drinkers and the birds. A solid block stays where you place it better than loose bait.
intro: In a farm store or a poultry house, rodents eat and spoil feed and disturb the birds. Controlling them takes bait that stays where you put it, and that is the idea behind a bait block fixed inside a station.

sections.heading: Why use a block instead of loose bait?
paragraphs: A block is heavy and solid, so it resists damp and handling better than loose bait. Rodents can carry or gnaw a block, but one held inside a station stays where you put it.
In a poultry house the birds, the feed and the drinkers are all close to the places rodents travel, which is why the blocks belong inside stations and nowhere else.
That also makes it easier to see which stations are being visited, and to replace only the bait that has been eaten.

sections.heading: How do I place the stations?
paragraphs: Look for droppings, gnaw marks, runways and burrows to find where rodents travel. Place bait stations along walls, near holes, behind stacked goods and in dark corners, and put the blocks inside so that children, pets and livestock cannot reach them.
Check the stations regularly, replace blocks that have been eaten, and move a station if there is no activity at that spot.

sections.heading: What should I prepare and avoid?
paragraphs: Use the blocks only inside bait stations, never on food or in food areas. Wear gloves, collect dead rodents, dispose of them safely and wash your hands afterwards. Check the PCPB registration number on the label and read the label before use. Prepare the building first:
bullets: Store grain, feed and produce on raised pallets, away from walls, in rodent-proof containers
Seal holes and gaps, and keep drains and doors closed or screened
Remove rubbish and clutter, and cut tall grass and bush near buildings

faq: Can I use the blocks in a poultry house?
They are sold for poultry houses as well as stores and farms. Use them only inside bait stations, away from feed, drinkers and the birds.
Why are bait blocks used in stations?
A block fixed inside a station is not scattered or carried off, and children, pets and livestock cannot reach it.
What size is the pack?
The product is sold as one pack. Check the pack for its size, and keep the blocks in their original pack, dry and locked away from children, pets and food.
closing: See the [[/p/syngenta-tatua-rat-and-mice-poison-blocks.html|Syngenta Tatua blocks product page]], browse [[/c/rodent-control.html|rodent control]], or read how to [[/blog/how-to-disinfect-a-poultry-house-kenya.html|disinfect a poultry house]].

title: Termites in timber and gardens: using Gradometer 480EC
description: Mchwa can weaken roof timbers and fence posts before damage shows. See what Gradometer 480EC termiticide treats in Kenya, and how to apply it safely.
answer: Gradometer 480EC is an emulsifiable concentrate termiticide with chlorpyrifos, used on timber in buildings, trees, fencing poles, wooden structures and termite nests in lawns and gardens. Dilute it with water exactly as the label directs, treat cut ends, joints and wood touching the soil, and wear full protective gear.
intro: Mchwa (termites) feed on wood, paper and other plant material, and they can weaken roof timbers, door frames, fence posts and furniture before the damage is clearly visible. Early treatment limits the damage and the cost of repairs.

sections.heading: What can Gradometer 480EC treat?
paragraphs: Gradometer 480EC contains 480 grams of chlorpyrifos per litre and comes in a 1 litre bottle. It is used where termites attack:
bullets: Timber in buildings and construction
Trees and fencing poles
Wooden structures such as sheds, posts and frames
Termite nests in lawns and gardens

sections.heading: How should I prepare and apply it?
paragraphs: It is an emulsifiable concentrate, so it is diluted with water as directed on the label. Use the label dilution for timber and for nests, and never mix it stronger than recommended.
Treat timber thoroughly, paying attention to cut ends, joints and the places where wood touches the soil. For a nest, follow the label instructions for reaching it and treating the soil around it.

sections.heading: What safety steps matter most?
paragraphs: Check the PCPB registration number on the label, and mix and apply exactly as directed. Wear gloves, a mask, goggles and protective clothing, and keep away from children, pets, food and water.
Chlorpyrifos is harmful to fish and aquatic life, so keep it away from streams, ponds, wells and drains. For buildings, consider a licensed pest control operator.
Store the product in its original closed bottle, in a cool, dry, locked place away from food and feed.

sections.heading: How do I stop termites coming back?
paragraphs: Treatment does not replace good housekeeping. Give termites fewer reasons to return:
bullets: Remove old stumps, dead wood and rotting timber from around buildings
Keep timber off the ground where possible, and keep it dry
Fix leaking pipes and drains that keep the soil damp
Inspect timber regularly for mud tubes, soft wood and flying termites

faq: Can I use it on a termite mound in my garden?
It is used for treating termite nests in lawns and gardens. Follow the label instructions for reaching the nest and treating the soil around it.
Is Gradometer 480EC ready to spray?
No. It is a concentrate, so you dilute it with water as directed on the label before use.
What are the signs of termites in timber?
Look for mud tubes, soft wood and flying termites, especially where timber touches the soil.
closing: See the [[/p/gradometer-480ec-termiticide-1-litre.html|Gradometer 480EC product page]], browse [[/c/termite-control.html|termite control]], or read our [[/blog/termite-control-at-home-kenya.html|termite control guide]].
